messages.author: 3d786d0214ec4ea3
messages.subject: Plot individual varying intercept
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to plot an individual varying intercept from my brms model but I cannot seem to find the correct name for that parameter. I can plot all varying intercepts for a random effect but I cannot plot one of them alone. I would like to plot just one or a few so that I may visualize them on a pairs plot since there are too many to include them all in a pairs plot. 

My model is: Larvae | trials(100) ~ (Treatment+Light.s+Hours)^2 + (1|Experiment/Replicate), family=binomial()

I can plot all varying intercepts for Experiment and Experiment:Replicate by
plot(model, pars="r_Experiment")

but when I try using the title of one of those plots as a parameter name (which is the same as the name I get when I run parnames(model)) to plot just that individual intercept, like this:
plot(model, pars=r_Experiment[June28,Intercept])

I get an error "Error: No valid parameters selected." June28 is the name of one of my experiments. 

Is there a better way to select a specific varying intercept for plotting?

Thanks,
Sam

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Plot individual varying intercept
parts: As explained in ?plot.brmsfit, pars is interpreted as a regular expression, by default. Thus, you either have to escape the special characters in the parameter name and write pars = "r_Experiment\\[June28,Intercept\\]" or set exact_match = TRUE.
